\subsection{SolarWM on continuously changing commanded attitude}
\label{sec:h04-solarwm-continuous}

The generator result says the released world models do not depict the tilt a path requires.
That claim rests on the reader, and it says nothing about whether the verifier can ever say
\emph{yes}.  This campaign asks the second question with the one released path-controlled model
that follows a changing attitude.  Twenty-two paths whose commanded bank changes continuously
over three seconds (arcs, S-turns, slaloms and figure-eight-like asymmetric S-turns at 5, 8, 10,
12 and 20 deg peak, plus climb-turn and accelerate-brake variants) were generated with the
flatness attitude (arm A), with a level camera (arm B) and with the roll mirrored (arm C),
three validation draws per cell, on six first frames (three ANWM city views and three
simulated scenes).  234 clips from SolarWM-5B at 480x864, 81 frames, four sampling steps.

\paragraph{Scoring.}
The frozen reader reads every frame; the required side is the \emph{commanded} path
differentiated at 1 kHz with the label-free window rule $0.5/f_{95}$, i.e. the generator is
granted its best case and no path is recovered from pixels.  The coherence tier is primary,
with the R2 axis-gain band and the 6.46 deg median residual reported beside it, and abstention
follows the frozen rules in their frozen order.  Accept means testable and not flagged by
coherence.

The campaign answers the question the held-bank grid could not.  Of 78 arm-A clips, 51 are
testable under the frozen abstention rules and **31 are accepted** (61\,\% of the testable
clips): with a continuously changing command, SolarWM-5B does produce clips the frozen
coherence tier passes.  Where it is accepted the depicted tilt is $0.95$ times the required
tilt (35 of the 51 testable clips lie in $[0.5, 1.5]$), so this is not only a shape match.

The two wrong arms are rejected outright: the level arm is flagged $64/64$ and the mirrored
arm $42/42$, both 100\,\%, against 39\,\% for arm A.  Sampling does not rescue anything: the
median residual moves by $0.04^\circ$ across three validation draws and one of 22 paths
changes class, so the pre-registered sampling criterion fails.

Two things temper the result.  The yaw control, a $+20^\circ$ rotation about world up that
leaves the tilt unchanged, is flagged $10/11$ times: read on the same frames it perturbs the
reader's estimated up by 2.3--4.0$^\circ$, enough to break the coherence tier on weak-signal
clips.  Arm A's acceptance is therefore more likely an underestimate than an overestimate, and
the 100\,\% rejections of arms B and C are far outside that perturbation.  The same-arm null
flags 6 of 66 draw pairs.  Second, acceptance depends on the first frame: nothing is accepted
on the simulated \emph{urban\_checker} or \emph{forest\_ridge} scenes, the two the reader is
known to misread, while the ANWM city views and the industrial scene accept 4--9 clips each.
The accelerate-brake paths abstain by construction, since the frozen tier needs two-axis
signal.
